### Historical audit: S0134, visible chunk 2 of 3

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/generic_rsi/C2/test/commons_155212263/trajectory.jsonl`. All citations below refer to this file; ranges are the supplied character offsets.

| Evidence | Observation |
|---|---|
| Goal and first build — student `model_request`, line 13 [0,162615) | The task was to reconstruct a single indoor photograph with separate editable meshes, matching viewpoint, framing, occlusion and materials. The student **interpreted** it as a historic metalworking shop; that semantic identification is not independently verified here. Code defined multiple benches and lathes, windows, an anvil, drawer, vice, tools and containers. |
| Structure and appearance — line 13 [0,162615); student `model_response`, line 15 [0,15264) | The programs group components into assets, including bench legs and aprons, lathe rails, axles, wheels and belts. They specify procedural wood and wall texture, emissive window panes, a world and area lights. Code-level grouping and intended support do not establish actual contact, connectivity or visual correctness. Object pose and placement are parameterized, not independently checked geometrically. |
| Camera exploration — line 13 [0,162615) | After step 1, the student estimated that wheel, bin and distant-bench landmarks were displaced and revised camera position and target while retaining the 39 mm lens. Step 2 reported `ok: true` and a render available. The student later claimed improved framing and cropping; these are student visual estimates, not independent measurements. |
| Surface revision — lines 15 [0,15264), 16 [0,15907) | The student diagnosed pale machinery and timber as merging, then submitted and executed darker iron, wood, rust and drawer colors, retaining the step-2 camera and lighting. The intended result was stronger silhouettes without moving landmarks. This was a nonempty, executed revision, not merely a proposal. |
| Validation and selection — `execution_result`, line 17 [0,57700); `select`, line 18 [0,58) | Step 3 returned `ok: true`, saved a render and blend file, and was selected. Steps 1 and 2 likewise reported successful renders in line 13. This is **formal execution success**, not proof of a correct reconstruction. No independent image or geometric assessment is visible in this chunk. |
| Input and autonomy — lines 13 [0,162615), 14 [0,3805) | The runner supplied reference/render images and general comparison instructions. No separate teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, or receipt/adoption of teacher advice is visible. The student made its own landmark estimates and revisions within the prescribed process; the recorded third session was read-only with zero tool calls. |

**Uncertainty and lessons.** Only this chunk is visible; the reference and rendered pixels are not available for independent inspection. Thus actual object coverage, part connections, pose, occlusions, texture fidelity, lighting and camera match remain unresolved, as does whether darkening improved the result. No technical interruption or algorithm failure is shown. Transferably, the trace demonstrates separating a camera-pose revision from a later material revision and testing each; the specific workshop interpretation, landmarks and color diagnosis are task-specific hypotheses, not verified facts.
